title: Consent (MSDS)
summary: The consent register - the general consent of every admission, the informed consents of operations, anaesthesia, transfusions, procedures and high-risk treatments in the patient's language, who decides for a patient who cannot, the doctor's emergency note, refusals and withdrawals, the scan of the signed form, and the written consent policy.
workflow: MSDS PRE indicators 72-75, COP 35 and 43, AAC 23
markdown:
# Consent (MSDS)

The Punjab Healthcare Commission's Minimum Service Delivery Standards (MSDS) check consent in every sampled record, and
score the indicator "not met" for a single record without it ("a medico-legal issue"):

* a **general consent** when the patient is admitted (72): the need for admission, the estimated stay and cost, the
  hospital's rules, the patient's duty to disclose, sharing with the health authorities where the law requires it;
* the hospital's **list of situations** that need a specific informed consent (73): anaesthesia, surgery, sterilization,
  termination of pregnancy, high-risk medicines...;
* each **informed consent** states the risks, benefits and alternatives, who will perform it and what it is, **in a
  language the patient understands**, signed by the patient or the next of kin **and by the professional** (74); its
  wording suits **every level of understanding** (35);
* a written **policy on who consents** for a patient who cannot (75), and its use;
* the consents to **anaesthesia** (35) and to the **operation** (43), taken by a qualified member of the team before it;
* the consent to a **transfusion** (AAC 23): a signed form, or the physician's note when an unconscious patient has
  nobody with them.

Who does what:

* **The admission desk** (`admissions_officer`), **ward and ER nurses** (`ward_nurse`, `triage_nurse`): the general
  consent (`consent.record`). The admission desk and ward nurses scan signed forms (`patient.document.upload`); in the
  ER the doctor or the admission desk uploads the scan.
* **Doctors** (`doctor`, `surgeon`, `anaesthetist`...): the informed consents. The database accepts an informed consent
  only from a doctor registered with the PMDC, and the consent to anaesthesia only from a doctor of the anaesthesia team
  (a pre-anaesthesia or anaesthesia clinical privilege, see [Surgical care](surgical-care.md)).
* **Quality Officer, Owner** (`consent.configure`, `consent.statistics.view`): the forms and their texts, the decision
  makers, the written policy, the register and the statistics.

Every consent is a row of the register with its number (`CN-2026-000123`), the text **as printed** in the language
chosen, what was explained, the decision and the stamp of who took it. States: `Draft` → `Given` | `Refused` |
`Cancelled`; `Given` → `Withdrawn` (not once its operation has started). A decided consent is final. Refresh screens on
`consent.updated`; the surgical record also receives `ot.clinical.updated` with `record: "Consent"`.

## 1. The policy (once, then yearly)

1. `GET /consent-forms?include_inactive=false`: the situations and their forms. Each form has a `category` (`General`,
   `Procedure`, `Anaesthesia`, `Transfusion`, `HighRiskTreatment`, `AgainstMedicalAdvice`, `Other`), `situations` (when
   it is needed), `taken_by` (`AnyStaff`, `Doctor`, `Anaesthetist`), `requires_witness`, and `texts`: the heading and
   the declaration per language with its `direction` (`rtl` for Urdu and Pakistan's other languages but English). The
   seed ships nine forms in **English and Urdu** in plain words (general consent, operation, anaesthesia, transfusion,
   invasive procedure, sterilization, termination of pregnancy, high-risk treatment, leaving against advice) as a
   starting point: the hospital adapts them and has its legal adviser approve them.
2. `POST /consent-forms {"code", "category", "title", "situations", "taken_by", "requires_witness", "sort_order",
   "texts": [{"language", "heading", "body"}]}` adds a situation; `PATCH /consent-forms/{form_id}` changes it or retires
   it (`is_active: false`); `PUT /consent-forms/{form_id}/texts/{language} {"heading", "body", "expected_version"?}`
   adds or rewrites a language (Punjabi, Saraiki, Pashto, Sindhi, Balochi). Consents already prepared keep the text they
   were printed with.
3. `GET /consent-decision-makers`: who decides for a patient who cannot, in order, for an adult (`adult_priority`) and
   for a child (`minor_priority`); null means "may not decide for that patient". Seeded from MSDS 74 ii: a court-appointed
   guardian, a person the patient appointed in writing, the spouse, an adult child, a parent, an adult brother or sister,
   another adult relative, the care provider (for a child: a parent first). `PATCH /consent-decision-makers/{relationship}
   {"description"?, "adult_priority"?, "minor_priority"?, "expected_version"?}` changes the order.
4. The rules are settings (`PUT /admin/settings/{key}`): `consent_adult_age` (18: the age of consent),
   `consent_valid_days` (30: an operation's consents older than this are taken again), `consent_scan_hours` (24: the
   signed paper is scanned within), `consent_emergency_second_doctor` (true: the emergency note needs a second doctor).
   The screens that take a consent never read these settings: each consent's `who_decides` (section 4) applies them to
   its patient.
5. `GET /consent-policy/pdf`: the written policy (MSDS 73 i, 75 i): the situations with their forms and languages, who
   decides for an adult and for a child, the rules, with lines for the medical director's approval.

## 2. What is still to do

`GET /consent-worklist?days=7&mine=false` lists, oldest first (`due_at`, `overdue`):

* `GeneralConsent`: an admission (reserved, Code Red or admitted) without its general consent;
* `OperationConsent`, `AnaesthesiaConsent`: an operation not signed in yet (coming up within `days`) without the
  consent to it or, with an anaesthetist, to the anaesthesia;
* `Scan`: a signed form not scanned into the record (`due_at` = the signature + `consent_scan_hours`).

`consent_id` is the draft already prepared (or the consent to scan). `mine`: the caller's admissions and operations
(an anaesthetist: every operation needing an anaesthesia consent) and the forms they took.

## 3. Preparing the form

1. Pick the form and the **language the patient understands** (only the form's `texts`).
2. `POST /consents {"form_code", "language", "admission_id"? | "booking_id"? | "er_visit_id"? | "ticket_id"? |
   "patient_id"?, "procedure_name"?, "performer_id"?, "performer_name"?, "risks"?, "benefits"?, "alternatives"?,
   "admission_need"?, "estimated_days"?, "estimated_cost"?}` with an `Idempotency-Key` header. The patient comes from the
   admission, operation or visit. A general consent needs `admission_id`. Prefilled:
   * the operation (`OPERATION`, category `Procedure`): the procedure and the surgeon ("Dr X and the surgical team");
   * the anaesthesia: "General anaesthesia for ..." from the assessment's planned technique, and its anaesthetist;
   * the general consent: the need for admission from the admission's reason.
   `CONSENT_TEXT_MISSING` (`details.available`): no text in that language.
   * The performer (`performer_id`) from `GET /staff/lookup`; the same on `PATCH /consents/{consent_id}`.
3. The draft's `missing` lists what the explanation still lacks: for an informed consent the procedure, who performs it,
   the risks, the benefits, the alternatives; for the general consent the need, the estimated stay (days) and cost.
   `PATCH /consents/{consent_id}` with the fields (and `language`: the form is printed again in it) completes it.
4. **Print it**: `GET /consents/{consent_id}/print-payload` (A4, `printer_role` `document`). `fields.consent` has the
   heading and the text as printed (`form_title`, `form_body`, one paragraph per line) and `direction`;
   `fields.explained` what was explained (blank lines where empty); `fields.signature_lines` the lines to sign;
   `barcode_svg` the consent number (for matching the scan). **The terminal prints Urdu**: lay out right-to-left
   languages yourself from `fields`, in the Nastaliq font bundled with the app (`dir="rtl"`, the consent number and
   CNIC in `<bdi>`); for them `text` and `pdf_url` are null, and `GET /consents/{consent_id}/pdf` answers
   `CONSENT_PDF_UNAVAILABLE`, since the server prints Latin-script languages only. The guide "Printing & hardware"
   (Urdu and right-to-left printouts) has the details. English prints from `text` or `pdf_url` too.
5. **Explain it** in words the patient understands; read it aloud when they cannot read; use an interpreter when
   needed; answer their questions; ask them to say it back in their own words. Have the paper signed or thumb-printed,
   with the witness when the form or a thumb impression needs one.

## 4. Recording the decision

**Given**: `POST /consents/{consent_id}/sign` with
The emergency note's second doctor (`second_doctor_id`) from `GET /staff/lookup?license_type=PMDC`.

* `signer`: `Patient` (their name by default), or `DecisionMaker` when the patient cannot decide, with
  `signer_relationship` (one `GET /consent-decision-makers` allows for this patient: `adult_priority` for an adult,
  `minor_priority` for a child), `signer_name`, `signer_cnic`, `signer_phone`, and `incapacity_reason` (`Minor`,
  `Unconscious`, `Confused`, `MentalIllness`, `Sedated`, `Other`);
* who that may be comes with the consent itself (`GET /consents/{consent_id}` and every answer of the consent),
  `who_decides`: the server applies the hospital's settings to this patient, the rule the decision is checked with
  (backend issue #39). `adult_age` (the age of consent), `patient_is_minor` (the patient's age is known and below it;
  an unknown age counts as an adult), `patient_may_sign` (false for a minor: offer only a decision maker),
  `decision_makers` (the relationships allowed for this patient, each with its `description` and `priority`, in the
  order to ask: offer these and no other) and `emergency_second_doctor` (the emergency note below needs the second
  doctor). Never classify the patient or hardcode an age on the terminal. A decision dated earlier (`decided_at`) is
  checked on its own date;
* `signer_mark`: `Signature` or `ThumbImpression` (then `witness_name` is required), `witness_name`, `witness_role`;
* `interpreter_name`, `read_to_patient`, `questions_answers` ("None asked" is an answer) and `understanding_confirmed`
  (both required: the evidence that the patient was informed, MSDS 35 ii, 43 iii);
* `decided_at` (default now; a few minutes of terminal clock drift are accepted, never later), `expected_version`.

The caller is the professional who explained it: their stamp (name, designation, PMDC number, date and time) is printed
on the consent (`obtained_stamp`, MSDS 74 iii, 147).

**The emergency note** (MSDS AAC 23 ii, COP 43): when the patient cannot decide, nobody can be reached and the
treatment cannot wait, the doctor signs with `{"mode": "EmergencyNote", "incapacity_reason", "emergency_note",
"second_doctor_id"}`: why it could not wait, and a second doctor registered with the PMDC (not the caller) who concurs
(setting `consent_emergency_second_doctor`), picked with `GET /staff/lookup?q=…&license_type=PMDC`.

**Refused** (an informed refusal): `POST /consents/{consent_id}/refuse` with the same signer fields and
`refusal_reason`, the reason in the patient's words; `mode: VerbalRefusal` when they refuse but will not sign (a witness
is required). For a patient leaving the hospital against advice use the form `AGAINST_ADVICE` and record it as given.

Errors: `CONSENT_INCOMPLETE` (`details.missing`: mark those fields), `CONSENT_SIGNER_INVALID` (a child deciding alone, a
relationship the policy does not allow, with `details.allowed`; the second doctor missing or the caller),
`CONSENT_TAKER_NOT_AUTHORIZED` (not a registered doctor; anaesthesia: not the anaesthesia team),
`CONSENT_STATE_INVALID` (already decided), `VALIDATION_ERROR` (a date in the future).

## 5. After the decision

1. **Scan the signed paper** (MSDS 74 ii: the signatures on file): upload it (or a photo, or the signature pad's image)
   as a patient document of type `Consent`: `POST /patients/{patient_id}/documents` (multipart: `file`,
   `doc_type=Consent`, `title`: the consent number), then `POST /consents/{consent_id}/scan {"document_id"}`. A later
   scan replaces it; the history keeps both. An emergency note needs no scan.
2. **Withdraw**: `POST /consents/{consent_id}/withdraw {"reason"}`: the patient changed their mind (or it was recorded in
   error); not once its operation has started (`CONSENT_STATE_INVALID`). Take a new consent if the treatment goes ahead.
   A **transfusion** consent withdrawn cancels at once every open blood request it covered; a unit already out stays on
   its request, the database refuses to issue or start blood on it (`BLOOD_CONSENT_REQUIRED`), and
   `blood.consent.withdrawn` tells the ward and the blood bank (see [blood transfusion](blood-transfusion.md)).
3. **Cancel a draft** entered in error (wrong form or patient): `POST /consents/{consent_id}/cancel {"reason"}`.

A decided consent is never edited (`CONSENT_STATE_INVALID`, also in the database).

## 6. Where the system requires them

* **The sign in of an operation** (`POST /ot/bookings/{booking_id}/safety-checks` with `SignIn`): the consent to the
  operation and, with an anaesthetist, to the anaesthesia, given within `consent_valid_days`, or `CONSENT_REQUIRED`.
  The surgical record shows them (`consents`, the parts `OperationConsent` and `AnaesthesiaConsent`, `next_step`).
* **The clinical discharge** (`POST /admissions/{admission_id}/discharge`): the general consent of the admission,
  given, refused or the emergency note, or `CONSENT_REQUIRED` (MSDS 72: every inpatient record holds it).
* **The medical record review** checks every sampled stay: `ADM_GENERAL_CONSENT` (given and scanned, or the emergency
  note) and `ADM_CONSENT` (each operation's consents given before its sign in and scanned; a transfusion the operative
  note records has its consent). See [Medical record review](medical-record-review.md).

## 7. The register and the statistics

* `GET /consents?patient_id&admission_id&booking_id&status&category&date_from&date_to&unscanned&limit`: newest first
  (the dates filter on the decision). `unscanned=true`: signed forms whose paper is not in the record.
* `GET /consents/{consent_id}`: everything, with the text as printed (logged as a patient-data access).
* `GET /consent-statistics?date_from&date_to` (`consent.statistics.view`): `measures`, each with `applicable`, `met`,
  `pct` and its MSDS reference: discharged admissions with the general consent (72), operations with the consent to the
  operation before the sign in (43) and to the anaesthesia (35), signed forms scanned (74 ii); then `by_category`
  (given, refused, withdrawn), `by_language`, `by_decider` (`Patient`, each relationship, `EmergencyNote`),
  `thumb_impressions`, `with_interpreter`, `read_aloud`.
